To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ACVRLI gene, which is mutated in hereditary hemorrhagic
telangiectasia (Type 2 HHT), was associated with clinically sporadic arterovenous dysplaslasias of the central nervous
system (AVMs, dural arterio-venous fistulas) but not with clinically sporadic intracranial saccular aneurysms.
we have identified an association between a polymorphism in intronic sequence of ACVRL1 and AVMs of the CNS.
the IVS3-35A/T polymorphisms of ACVRL1 are significantly associated with the formation and development of AVM and DAVF of CNS, which is a common clinical manifestation in patients with HHH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a new genetic factor associated with the formation and development of arteriovenous vascular dysplasias of the CNS.
the identification of a genetic factor that is associated with a clinically sporadic form of a CNS manifestation in a disease that is caused by germlinemutations in the ENG or ACVRL1 genes.
the genetic background of vascular malformative lesions of the CNS and provides new insights into the etiopathogenesis of AVMs
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a germline ACVRL1 mutation is a rare cause of sporadic AVM, and the ACVRL 1 polymorphism IVS3 - 35A/T is associated with a 1.7-fold increased risk of sporadic CNS AVM.
ACVRL1 is involved in the formation of sporadic AVM/DAVF, but not aneurismal lesions, and that this involvement is mediated by the IVS3-35A/T polymorphisms.
the IVS3-35A/T polymorphisms in the intron 3 region of the ACV RL1 gene are associated with the formation and/or the development of A VMs of the CNS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified a sequence variation in the 3' end of the ACV RL1 gene (IVS 3 - 35A/T), which is statistically significantly associated with the development and formation of clinically sporadic AVM/DAVF in the CNS.
we have identified a polymorphism in the ACVRL gene that is associated with the development in humans of sporadic arterio-venous dysplasia of the CNS.
we have identified a polymorphism in intronic region of the ACVLR1 gene (IVS3 -35 A/T) associated with the development AVMs and dural arterovenous fistulas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a genetic variant of the HHT Type 2 (ACVRL1) gene is associated with the development and formation of clinically sporadic variants (AVMs and DAVFs) of vascular malformative lesions of the CNS, which are the most common manifestations of HHT.
the ACVRL 1 gene polymorphims may be a marker for the development of AWMs and DAVF of the CNS.
the ACVRL-1 gene may be associated with the formation and development of sporadic CNS AVMs and that this gene may also play a role in the formation and development in sporadic CNS aneurysms.
